I also grepped for uses of the divisor declarations; the only user is CurvePlaceSectionDivisor.lean. The ℂ in orderAt_finite_support and divisor is not needed by their proofs, so it can be generalised to any field. divisor_degree_eq_euler_difference really does depend on ℂ through euler_difference_eq_sum_zero_orders, so I did not flag it. mem_zero_support_iff_not_isUnit and orderAt_eq_zero_of_not_mem are already general. I could not compile anything, so the generalisation is untested. One elaboration dependency to check: the type universe of K (FiniteCurveZeros uses `K : Type`, and ℂ is in Type).

findings.problem: The finiteness of the support of orderAt, and the divisor and divisor_apply built from it, are stated only for proper schemes over ℂ. The proof never uses ℂ. It uses `finite_subscheme_of_curve p hd _ ...`, `zeroPoint_ne_generic` and `orderAt_eq_zero_of_not_mem`, and `finite_subscheme_of_curve` is already stated for an arbitrary field K. The ℂ-specific hypothesis is imported from the Euler-characteristic theorem, which does not apply to these declarations. This needlessly excludes curves over other fields, such as ℚ, finite fields or ℝ.
findings.proposed_change: Add `{K : Type} [Field K]` to the variables and state the lemma as `theorem orderAt_finite_support (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) [IsProper p] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (hDVR : ...) (L : LineBundle X) (s : GlobalSections X L.sheaf) (hs : s ≠ 0) : (Function.support (orderAt hDVR L s)).Finite`. The proof stays the same, since the call `finite_subscheme_of_curve p hd _ (SectionZeroIdeal.zeroIdeal_ne_bot L s hs)` is K-generic. Likewise state `divisor` and `divisor_apply` over a general field K. `divisor_degree_eq_euler_difference` can remain at ℂ, since it needs `euler_difference_eq_sum_zero_orders`. At the call site, ℂ is then just K := ℂ.
findings.benefit: The divisor of a section of a line bundle on a proper curve becomes available over any base field, not just ℂ, with no new mathematics. The definition no longer carries a spurious ℂ dependency, and the Euler-characteristic degree formula is the only ℂ-specific result.
